Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies:
Amrize Building Envelope LLC (Amrize) is dedicated to protecting employees, the community, and the environment from highly hazardous incidents through safely operating our facility.
Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies:
The facility's overall approach and commitment to chemical safety is demonstrated by 1) the management, training, procedure, and maintenance systems in place at the facility, and 2) the hazard assessment, prevention program and emergency response provisions implemented specifically for the covered flammables in response to the RMP requirement. The management structure and oversight to ensure safety is documented in the facility's RMP and includes compliance with applicable regulations, codes and standards (OSHA PSM Standard and US EPA 40 CFR 68).
Source and Federal Regulated Substances Description:
The Rockland facility manufactures adhesives for use in the building industry. The facility houses manufacturing, office, and warehouse areas. Other structures on the site include above ground storage tanks and associated piping and instrumentation.  The vicinity of the area is light commercial/industrial area. 
The processes which trigger applicability to the Risk Management Plan (RMP) are the above ground flammable propellant storage tanks associated with the pressurized container filling operation and storage of finished product. There are three RMP listed chemicals including a flammable blend (isobutane/propane), methyl ether and isopentane. The chemicals arrive by tanker truck, are unloaded and stored in outdoor above ground horizontal tanks. The chemicals are processed in the Gas House where they are either blended and packaged into pressurized canisters or are repackaged in the canisters for use as spray adhesives. The filled cylinders are stored in a caged area of the warehouse and shipped out via truck.

General Accidental Release Prevention Program and Chemica

l-Specific Prevention Steps:
The facility has implemented a Program Level 3 Program for the covered process, as required by the RMP rule, in accordance with the US EPA guidance. The covered chemicals are also regulated under OSHAs Process Safety Management (PSM) regulation. Therefore, the Rockland facility has a comprehensive PSM/RMP Prevention Program. These prevention program provisions are specifically intended to minimize the probability and/or consequence of any accidental release from the facility and include such measures as process hazards analysis, operating procedures, training, contractors, pre-start-up safety, mechanical integrity, hot work permit, management of change, incident investigation, emergency planning and response, and compliance audits. The facility prevention program is an ongoing system based on periodic training, incident investigations, audits, procedure revisions, and RMP updates as required to reflect facility change and RMP requirements.
Five-year Accident History:
The facility has had no RMP reportable accidents or releases of the covered chemicals.
 
Emergency Response Program:
The facility has developed and implemented a detailed Integrated Contingency Plan (ICP) which includes our Emergency Action Plan. The ICP addresses emergency and incident notification reporting, emergency health care, emergency response actions, training requirements, and incident prevention program.  The Rockland facility is considered a defensive responder and will rely on outside responders and resources in the event of an emergency. The facility has ongoing coordination activities with the Rockland Fire Department to ensure timely communication and a safe response to any accidental release from the facility.
 
Planned changes to improve safety:
The facility is committed to ensuring its operations are safe and in accordance with all RMP requirements and has established a senior manager responsible for RMP development, implementation, and compliance. This m

anager is committed to maintain the safety of the RMP covered process through active adherence to the appropriate procedures and codes. To ensure that the appropriate changes occur as necessary to maintain/improve safety, ongoing hazard reviews, training, audits, maintenance, and investigations will be conducted as required by RMP. Updates to the RMP will be completed as necessary in response to these activities.
As documented in this submittal, the RMP for the facility has been completed in accordance with all 40 CFR 68 requirements, and the facility has certified compliance. Amrize takes pride in and is committed to conducting business in strict conformity with all applicable laws in a safe and responsible manner. The very highest priority is placed on the health and safety of Amrize's teammates and the community in which we conduct business.
